newsitem.title: UK: Bass says continues to perform well.
newsitem.headline: Bass says continues to perform well.

text.p: British brewer-to-hotel group Bass Plc continues to perform well overall despite facing intense competition in its markets, chairman Sir Ian Prosser said on Wednesday.
"The forecasts for economic growth around the world are encouraging," he added.
The company reported a 10 percent increase to 318 million pounds in its profits before tax for the six months to April 12, 1997 driven by its managed pubs and 2,200 Holiday Inn empire.
Brokers had forecast profits of between 305 and 325 million pounds($537.8 million). The dividend payout was also in line with expectations at 8.3 pence per share.

Group turnover grew by 6.8 percent to 2.693 billion pounds. Holiday Inn's improved operating profit 5.3 percent to 80 million pounds, or 10.2 percent in dollar terms as average room rates in America rose sharply.

Bass' 2,812 managed pubs grew trading profits by 12.6 percent to 116 million while the group's leisure division, which includes Gala bingo halls and Coral betting shops, raised protis by 11.4 percent to 39 million.
Profits from its beer business were 6.9 percent higher in the first half of 1997 than in 1996 at 77 million, with key brands Carling Black Label and Worthington draught bitter performing strongly.
